title: Scikit-learn Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Scikit-learn. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: What is y in this example?
questions.explanation: A feature is an input measurement. A label is the known answer in a teaching example. Scikit-learn usually expects a table of feature rows. The output is 4 4. Each one-value feature row has one matching class label. The labels are fictional groups.

questions.question: Which method learns from the examples?
questions.explanation: A classifier chooses a group label. fit lets the model learn from examples. A decision tree splits inputs using learned thresholds. The predictions are [0, 1]. The shallow tree separates the low and high numbers in this toy dataset.

questions.question: How many examples are held out?
questions.explanation: A test set holds examples kept out of model fitting. It gives a better check than only asking about examples the model already saw. The output is 8 2. Two examples are held out. stratify helps preserve the class proportions for this split.

questions.question: What does this baseline always choose?
questions.explanation: A baseline is a simple result to compare against. DummyClassifier can always choose the most frequent training class. The output is [0, 0]. This baseline ignores the feature values and chooses the common class.

questions.question: How many predictions are correct?
questions.explanation: Accuracy is the fraction of labels predicted correctly. It can be misleading when one class is much more common than another. The result is 0.75 because three of four predictions match.

questions.question: What do rows represent here?
questions.explanation: A confusion matrix counts correct and incorrect class choices. With labels [0, 1], rows are true labels and columns are predicted labels. The result is [[1, 1], [0, 2]]. One true 0 was predicted as 1; both true 1 values were correct.

questions.question: Which data should fit the scaler?
questions.explanation: Scaling puts features on a chosen numeric scale. Fit the scaler on training data, then use that fitted scaler on other data. The middle value becomes 0.0 because it equals the training mean. Other values are measured relative to the learned spread.

questions.question: What runs first in this pipeline?
questions.explanation: A pipeline applies preparation and a model in the intended order. It helps use the same preparation for fitting and prediction. The result is [0, 1]. The pipeline scales the input and then asks the nearest-neighbour model for labels.

questions.question: What does regression predict?
questions.explanation: Regression predicts a number instead of a class. LinearRegression fits a straight-line relationship to the examples. The output is 8.0. The training examples follow the exact rule output = 2 times input.

questions.question: What is the mean absolute error here?
questions.explanation: Mean absolute error averages the size of prediction mistakes without keeping their plus or minus signs. The result is 0.5. The absolute errors are 1 and 0, whose average is one half.

questions.question: How many validation scores are produced?
questions.explanation: Cross-validation trains and evaluates on several train/validation splits. It gives more than one estimate, but still needs careful data grouping. The output is 3 because three validation folds were used. Iris is included with scikit-learn; no download is needed.

questions.question: What does max_depth limit?
questions.explanation: A model setting chosen before fitting is a hyperparameter. max_depth limits how many splits a tree can make along a path. The result is 1. The tree learned one split level for this dataset. A larger limit allows more complex rules.
